name: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36); first posted arXiv:2303.11366, Mar 2023
authors_affiliation: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Edward Berman (Northeastern University); Ashwin Gopinath (MIT); Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao (Princeton University). Lead author: Noah Shinn (Northeastern University).
task_domain: decision-making / agents (sequential decision-making, knowledge-intensive reasoning QA, and code generation). Covers embodied text-world (AlfWorld), multi-hop QA (HotPotQA), and code (HumanEval/MBPP/LeetcodeHard).
problem_setting: Interactive, online, single-agent setting where an LLM acts as a goal-driven agent in external environments (games/TextWorld, compilers/interpreters, Wikipedia API). The agent learns from trial-and-error across multiple episodes without any weight updates or fine-tuning; instead it relies on verbal (linguistic) reinforcement. Supervision is sparse: a binary/scalar success signal comes from the environment, ground-truth match (EM), self-generated unit tests, or an LLM/heuristic self-evaluator. The same task is retried over a bounded number of trials until the Evaluator deems the trajectory correct or max trials is reached.
what_is_retrieved: experiences: the agent's own verbal self-reflections (free-text lessons distilled from prior failed trials) stored in an episodic long-term memory buffer, conditioned on in subsequent trials of the SAME task.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes itself (self-reflection text accumulated across trials). It is not a static external corpus; the agent generates and stores its own reflective notes, then re-reads them. (The ReAct-based variant additionally queries a Wikipedia API for external context, but the Reflexion-specific 'retrieval' is from self-written episodic memory.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither a fixed top-k ranking nor a completeness objective in the IR sense. The memory is small (bounded sliding window of 1-3 reflections) and ALL stored reflections are injected into context as the agent's accumulated experience; there is no ranked similarity retrieval over a large store. [uncertain] (no explicit retrieval-ranking objective is defined).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: partial - all stored reflections re-loaded each trial rather than similarity-retrieved; Reuse: yes - past reflections condition the next trial; Revise: yes - the agent generates a new reflection / revised plan; Retain: yes - new reflection appended to memory]. Realizes a CBR-like trial-revise-retain loop but over self-reflections, not problem-solution cases.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is framed as 'verbal reinforcement learning' / policy optimization in natural language, drawing on RL (Sutton & Barto) and in-context policy iteration (Brooks et al., 2022).
retrieval_unit: thought-step / experience: a free-text self-reflection summarizing what went wrong in the prior trajectory and an improved plan (verbal experience feedback sr_t). Short-term memory additionally holds the full current/recent trajectory.
index_source: Growing episodic memory induced online at test time: built by the agent during the retry loop for each task; frozen across tasks (no cross-task memory transfer). Bounded by a maximum capacity Omega (typically 1-3 stored experiences).
index_structure_topology: Flat append-only list (memory buffer mem = [sr_0, sr_1, ...]) truncated to the most recent 1-3 entries (sliding window). No vector index or graph; the paper explicitly suggests future work could add vector-embedding or SQL databases.
retriever_type: None / trivial: there is no learned or similarity-based retriever. The full (truncated) memory buffer is concatenated into the prompt. Effectively recency-windowed read-all rather than a ranked retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf): no retriever is trained. The signal that shapes memory CONTENT is the environment reward amplified into verbal feedback by the Self-Reflection LLM, but the read/selection mechanism itself is not learned.
query_construction: No explicit query is constructed for retrieval; the agent simply conditions the next trial's generation on its stored reflections plus the current task/state observation. The verbal self-reflection is generated from {trajectory tau_t, scalar reward r_t, prior memory}.
query_granularity: task-level / trajectory-level: reflections are generated once per trial (after a full trajectory) and re-injected at the start of the next trial; there is no per-step retrieval query.
when_to_retrieve: iterative across trials: the accumulated memory is re-read at the start of every new trial of the same task. Writing a reflection is triggered after each failed/evaluated trial (or, for AlfWorld heuristic, when stuck >3 repeats or >30 actions).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule per trial for reading memory; for writing, the trigger is the Evaluator's failure signal (binary success/fail from environment, exact-match grading, self-generated unit-test results, LLM self-evaluation, or hand-written heuristics detecting repeated actions / inefficient planning).
reranking: None. No reranking stage; the bounded memory is used as-is.
retrieved_context_refinement: Distillation at write time rather than at read time: the Self-Reflection LLM compresses a long failed trajectory + sparse reward into a concise actionable verbal lesson before storing. At read time, the buffer is truncated to the last 1-3 experiences (window-based pruning). No rerank/distractor-filtering of retrieved items.
index_content_separation: N/A. Short-term memory holds full trajectory detail while long-term memory holds distilled reflections, a loose separation, but not a lightweight-index-then-load-content design.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: stored self-reflections are concatenated into the LLM Actor's context as additional 'self-hint' guidance, acting as a semantic gradient that steers the next trial's actions/answers. No weight updates.
planning_integration: Per-trial conditioning / retrieve-then-act: at the start of each new episode the agent reads its long-term reflective memory plus short-term trajectory, then re-plans and re-acts (via CoT or ReAct). Memory influences the whole next rollout rather than being injected at individual planning sub-steps.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-trial / per-answer: reflection is woven in once per episode (between trials), not per CoT-step or per-tool-call. Within a trial the underlying Actor may be ReAct (per-step thought-action), but the Reflexion memory mechanism operates at the episode boundary.
adaptation_mechanism: execution-feedback-driven revision: the retrieved verbal reflection prompts the LLM Actor to adapt its plan/actions in the next trial; revision is guided by sparse reward + self-critique rather than verbatim ICL reuse of a stored solution.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled free-text strategy / lesson written in the first person (verbal self-reflection summarizing the failure and an improved plan). Plus the raw recent trajectory in short-term memory.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy/insight (an actionable lesson abstracted from a failed trajectory), more abstract than a raw trajectory but task-specific rather than a reusable cross-task skill or workflow.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Self-reflection / self-evaluation acts as the relevance/quality filter: the Self-Reflection and Evaluator LLMs (or heuristics, EM grading, self-generated unit tests) decide what feedback to store. For code, the paper analyzes false-positive/false-negative unit tests; it notes preference for false negatives. No retriever-aware training or distractor-filtering of stored items. Memory window truncation limits accumulation of stale context.
memory_type: episodic (long-term episodic memory buffer of verbal self-reflections, plus short-term trajectory memory).
write_back: True: after each trial the Self-Reflection model produces a new reflection sr_t that is appended to the episodic memory buffer mem.
online_growth: True (within a task / across trials): the memory grows during deployment as the agent retries a task, bounded by max capacity Omega (1-3). It does NOT persist/grow across different tasks (memory is per-task).
write_back_trigger: Reflective, after self-critique of an evaluated (typically failed) trial: triggered by the Evaluator's sparse reward signal (environment binary success, EM grading, self-generated unit-test failure, LLM self-evaluation, or AlfWorld heuristics for repeated actions/inefficient planning). Effectively writes on failure / not-yet-passed trials.
failure_experience_usage: Failure-centric corrective reflections: Reflexion explicitly learns from prior FAILINGS - verbal feedback distills what went wrong and how to improve, then conditions future trials on these corrective lessons. This failure-driven self-reflection is the core mechanism (ablation shows it adds ~8% over episodic-memory-only on HotPotQA and 60->68% on HumanEval Rust).
memory_evolution_update: Append-only with sliding-window forgetting/pruning: new reflections are appended; the buffer is truncated to the most recent Omega (1-3) experiences. Stored entries themselves are not mutated/merged/overwritten.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Reflexion frames the policy as 'memory encoding + LLM parameters' and performs natural-language policy optimization, but the case/memory selection is fixed (read-all-within-window), not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. Verbal reinforcement substitutes for gradient-based RL but does not learn a retriever.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private episodic memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework experience sharing.
benchmarks: AlfWorld (134 environments, 6 task types); HotPotQA (Wikipedia multi-hop QA, 100 questions evaluated); HumanEval (Python and Rust); MBPP (Python and Rust); LeetcodeHardGym (new benchmark: 40 Leetcode hard-rated questions across 19 programming languages, released after Oct 8 2022 GPT-4 cutoff). Rust translations via MultiPL-E.
benchmark_family: embodied (ALFWorld); multi-hop QA (HotPotQA); code (HumanEval / MBPP / LeetcodeHard).
baselines: ReAct (decision-making and QA); Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and CoT with ground-truth context CoT(GT) (reasoning); episodic-memory-only ablation (EPM, no self-reflection); base single-sample code generation with GPT-4; prior SOTA code methods: CodeT+GPT-3.5/Codex; reported prev-SOTA GPT-4 pass@1. Conceptually contrasted with Self-Refine, Self-Debugging, CodeRL, AlphaCode.
key_metrics: Task success rate / cumulative tasks solved (AlfWorld); exact-match accuracy over trials (HotPotQA); pass@1 accuracy (HumanEval/MBPP/LeetcodeHard); plus test-execution diagnostics (TP/FN/FP/TN, false-positive rate).
headline_result: 91.0% pass@1 on HumanEval (Python) with GPT-4 + Reflexion, surpassing the prior GPT-4 SOTA of 80.1%. Additional headline gains: AlfWorld +22% absolute (ReAct+Reflexion solves 130/134 tasks in 12 trials), HotPotQA +20% (~+14% over CoT(GT) without ground-truth answers).
ablations: (1) HotPotQA reasoning ablation: CoT(GT) baseline -> +episodic memory (EPM, most recent trajectory) -> +self-reflection; self-reflection adds an 8% absolute boost over the episodic-memory-only advantage, showing refinement-only is weaker than self-reflection-guided refinement. (2) Code ablation on 50 hardest HumanEval-Rust problems with GPT-4: Base 0.60; test-generation-omission (reflect without unit tests) 0.52 (worse than base); self-reflection-omission (tests but no verbal reflection) 0.60 (no gain over base); full Reflexion (tests + reflection) 0.68. Shows both unit-test grounding and verbal self-reflection are necessary, and they cooperate. (3) AlfWorld: failure-type analysis showing ReAct-only converges at ~22% hallucination rate while Reflexion recovers.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (success rate, pass@1, accuracy) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) since there is no ranked retriever. Code experiments do report unit-test confusion-matrix diagnostics (TP/FN/FP/TN) as an auxiliary process analysis.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final success/accuracy across trials), but with process-level analysis: learning curves over 12 trials, failure-type classification of AlfWorld trajectories, and unit-test false-positive/false-negative rates for code.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Positioned as lightweight vs gradient-based RL: no fine-tuning, learns within a handful of trials (e.g., ~12 trials in AlfWorld). Memory bounded to 1-3 experiences to fit LLM context limits. No detailed API-cost/latency/token-count budget table is reported. [uncertain] on precise compute/$ figures.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget-capped sliding window: long-term memory truncated to the last Omega = 1-3 self-reflections (AlfWorld and HotPotQA use 3; programming uses max 1) explicitly to respect maximum LLM context length. Code test suite capped at n<=6 self-generated unit tests.
benchmark_construction_and_size: LeetcodeHardGym (introduced by this paper): an interactive code-generation RL gym of 40 Leetcode hard-rated questions across 19 programming languages, all released after the GPT-4 pre-training cutoff (Oct 8, 2022) to avoid leakage; answer-verifiable via execution. Best reported: GPT-4 7.5% pass@1, Reflexion 15.0% pass@1 (Python), signaling high difficulty.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023) as the underlying action generator; Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., 2022) as reasoning Actor; in-context policy iteration (Brooks et al., 2022) inspiring the memory component; RL formulation (Sutton & Barto, 2018); MultiPL-E (Cassano et al., 2022) for Rust translation; self-generated unit tests akin to CodeT.
contrasts_with: Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023, single-generation, no persistent memory), Self-Debugging (Chen et al., 2023), CodeRL (Le et al., 2022), AlphaCode (Li et al., 2022), CodeT (Chen et al., 2022); gradient-based/weight-updating reinforcement learning; beam-search self-evaluation (Xie et al., 2023). Distinguished by persistent episodic memory of self-reflections + self-reflection step (vs blind retry/refine).
lineage: Group F (decision-making / memory / RL-style agents). A foundational early (2023) work in the experience/episodic-memory lineage of LLM agents: verbal/linguistic reinforcement over self-written episodic memory, a precursor to later experience-replay, skill-library, and case-based memory agents.
